comments.body: @sepo-agent /answer is adding route_overrides a lot of work?

Not a lot for basic `route_overrides`; moderate if we also make review lanes fully policy-driven.

The simple version is straightforward:

- Add `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` parser/resolver, modeled after existing JSON policy helpers like memory/rubrics/schedule.
- Resolve `default + route_overrides[route]` into `{ provider, model, reasoning_effort }`.
- Thread those values through `resolve-agent-provider` / `run-agent-task` / `run.ts`.
- Add tests and docs.

That handles single-agent routes cleanly: `answer`, `implement`, `fix-pr`, `orchestrator`, `self-approve`, `install`, etc.

The only part that can grow is `review`, because today it has a static two-lane matrix: Claude review + Codex review, then synthesis. Supporting `route_overrides.review.lanes` means either generating the matrix dynamically or adding a resolver step that emits lane config JSON. That is doable, just more workflow churn and snapshot tests.

I’d phase it:

1. First PR: support `default` and `route_overrides` for single-agent routes plus review synthesis.
2. Second PR only if needed: make reviewer lanes configurable.

So: not a big architectural lift, but I would avoid combining provider policy, model policy, display footer, and dynamic review matrix all in one change.
